decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Quantities, Functions and Elementary Geometry
decks.description: Build reusable mathematical literacy from the beginning.

outcomes.description: Calculate with fractions, ratios, units, powers and scientific notation.
Solve and rearrange linear, quadratic and simultaneous algebraic equations.
Interpret graphs and manipulate exponential, logarithmic and trigonometric functions.
Solve Euclidean similarity, coordinate, area, volume and angle problems.

includes: Arithmetic, algebra, elementary geometry and function representations

practice: Mixed multistep quantitative problems and graph construction

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Proof and Sets
decks.description: Transition from calculation to justified mathematical arguments.

outcomes.description: Translate statements using quantifiers and distinguish implication from equivalence.
Reason about sets, relations, functions and countability.
Construct direct, contrapositive and contradiction proofs; diagnose invalid arguments.
Prove recursive and finite claims using induction and invariants.

includes: Elementary mathematical language and proof construction

practice: Write and peer-critique complete proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Linear Algebra
decks.description: Compute with linear systems and explain their structure.

outcomes.description: Solve linear systems and interpret rank, nullity and invertibility.
Construct bases and prove elementary claims about linear maps.
Calculate eigenstructures and distinguish diagonalizable from defective operators.
Use projections, least squares and singular-value decomposition geometrically.

includes: Real and complex vectors, matrices, inner products and elementary proofs

practice: Hand calculations, geometric explanations and matrix experiments

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Single-Variable Calculus
decks.description: Model continuous change and accumulation computationally.

outcomes.description: Evaluate limits and distinguish continuity, divergence and asymptotic behavior.
Differentiate functions and solve rate, approximation and optimization problems.
Evaluate definite and improper integrals and explain the fundamental theorem.
Test series convergence and construct Taylor approximations with error bounds.

includes: Computational differential and integral calculus with series

practice: Modeling problems and symbolic-numerical cross-checks

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Multivariable and Vector Calculus
decks.description: Analyze change and integration in several dimensions.

outcomes.description: Calculate Jacobians, gradients and Hessians; classify constrained extrema.
Evaluate multiple integrals using coordinate transformations and Jacobians.
Compute line and surface integrals, divergence and curl.
Apply and justify Green, Gauss and Stokes theorems under stated hypotheses.

includes: Euclidean differential calculus and vector integral theorems

practice: Geometric field problems and coordinate-change calculations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Discrete Structures and Counting
decks.description: Develop finite mathematical models and arguments.

outcomes.description: Count constrained arrangements using bijections, inclusion-exclusion and generating functions.
Prove elementary graph properties and analyze trees, paths and matchings.
Solve recurrences and bound their asymptotic growth.
Compute congruences, greatest common divisors and modular inverses.

includes: Finite combinatorics, graph foundations and modular arithmetic

practice: Combinatorial proofs and finite-model construction

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Probability Models
decks.description: Calculate and interpret uncertainty without measure-theoretic prerequisites.

outcomes.description: Calculate event probabilities, conditional probabilities and Bayesian updates.
Construct discrete, continuous and joint distributions and transform variables.
Calculate expectations, variances, covariance and conditional expectation.
Apply laws of large numbers and central-limit approximations appropriately.

includes: Elementary counting taught locally; computational probability and limit interpretation

practice: Derivations and simulation checks of probability models

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Statistical Inference and Study Design
decks.description: Draw qualified conclusions from sampled data.

outcomes.description: Construct point estimates, confidence intervals and bootstrap uncertainty assessments.
Select hypothesis tests and interpret multiplicity, power and effect sizes.
Fit linear and generalized linear models and diagnose misspecification.
Design randomized or observational studies addressing confounding and sampling bias.

includes: Applied inference, regression, resampling and causal design principles

practice: Analyze real datasets with documented assumptions and residual checks

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Ordinary Differential Equations
decks.description: Translate changing systems into solvable dynamical models.

outcomes.description: Formulate and solve separable and first-order linear initial-value problems.
Solve forced linear differential equations and interpret resonance.
Solve linear systems and classify equilibria using eigenvalues.
Implement Euler and Runge-Kutta stepping and assess local error.

includes: ODE modeling, exact solutions and elementary numerical stepping

practice: Compare analytic, graphical and numerical solutions

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Numerical Analysis
decks.description: Choose and validate algorithms for approximate mathematical computation.

outcomes.description: Distinguish conditioning, rounding error, consistency and numerical stability.
Implement direct and iterative linear solvers with residual analysis.
Analyze root finding, interpolation and numerical quadrature errors.
Compare adaptive and stiff ODE integrators through convergence tests.

includes: Floating-point analysis and numerical linear, nonlinear and differential problems

practice: Implement algorithms and construct adversarial numerical test cases

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Real Analysis
decks.description: Rebuild calculus with rigorous convergence arguments.

outcomes.description: Prove sequence and series results using completeness and compactness.
Prove continuity and uniform continuity results with explicit quantifiers.
Prove differentiation and Riemann integration theorems and construct counterexamples.
Determine when limits interchange with continuity, differentiation or integration.

includes: Real-number completeness and rigorous one-variable analysis

practice: Full theorem proofs and counterexample construction

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Groups, Rings and Fields
decks.description: Study algebraic structure through homomorphisms and quotients.

outcomes.description: Prove group-action, quotient and Sylow results and classify small examples.
Analyze ideals, quotient rings, factorization and polynomial rings.
Construct field extensions and calculate algebraic degrees and finite fields.

includes: Proof-based group, ring and field foundations

practice: Structural proofs and explicit finite computations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Topological Spaces
decks.description: Generalize continuity and geometric structure beyond coordinates.

outcomes.description: Construct metric and topological spaces and test continuity.
Prove compactness and separation results and distinguish their hypotheses.
Analyze connectedness, path connectedness and local properties.
Construct product and quotient spaces using universal characterizations.

includes: Metric and general topology with examples and counterexamples

practice: Topology proofs and explicit quotient-space constructions

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Complex Analysis
decks.description: Develop analytic function theory and contour methods.

outcomes.description: Derive Cauchy-Riemann conditions and consequences of complex differentiability.
Prove and apply Cauchy integral results under appropriate hypotheses.
Classify singularities and evaluate integrals using residues.
Construct conformal maps and solve elementary harmonic boundary problems.

includes: Complex numbers introduced explicitly; holomorphic functions and contour integration

practice: Contour calculations and analytic proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Number Theory
decks.description: Connect arithmetic problems to algebraic and analytic methods.

outcomes.description: Prove divisibility and congruence theorems using arithmetic functions.
Prove quadratic reciprocity and solve quadratic congruences.
Solve selected Diophantine equations using descent and continued fractions.
Compute algebraic integers, norms and ideal factorizations in quadratic fields.
Derive elementary prime bounds and Euler-product identities.

includes: Elementary arithmetic and first algebraic and analytic number-theory methods
excludes: Proof of the prime number theorem

practice: Arithmetic proofs and computational investigations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Optimization Theory and Algorithms
decks.description: Characterize optima and choose reliable solution methods.

outcomes.description: Prove convexity and establish sufficient conditions for global optimality.
Derive constrained optimality conditions and identify constraint-qualification failures.
Formulate linear and convex duals and interpret duality gaps.
Implement gradient, Newton and proximal methods with convergence diagnostics.

includes: Finite-dimensional smooth and elementary nonsmooth convex optimization

practice: Proofs and constrained optimization projects

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Nonlinear Dynamical Systems
decks.description: Analyze qualitative behavior when exact solutions are unavailable.

outcomes.description: Establish local stability and construct Lyapunov arguments.
Classify elementary local bifurcations and periodic-orbit behavior.
Analyze iterated maps, invariant sets and fixed-point stability.
Distinguish chaos from noise using sensitive dependence and invariant diagnostics.

includes: Finite-dimensional flows and maps; qualitative and numerical analysis

practice: Phase portraits, bifurcation continuation and analytical proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Logic and Mathematical Foundations
decks.description: Study formal deduction and its limitations.

outcomes.description: Construct first-order languages, structures and formal derivations.
Prove soundness and explain a complete Henkin-style completeness proof.
Derive incompleteness consequences from arithmetization and diagonalization.
Use ZFC axioms to reason about ordinals, cardinals and choice.

includes: First-order metatheory and axiomatic set-theory foundations

practice: Formal derivations and metatheorem reconstructions

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Measure and Lebesgue Integration
decks.description: Develop integration on general measurable spaces.

outcomes.description: Construct measures from outer measures and identify measurable functions.
Construct the Lebesgue integral and compare it with Riemann integration.
Prove and apply monotone, dominated and Fatou convergence results.
Apply product integration and Radon-Nikodym derivatives with explicit hypotheses.

includes: Measure construction, integration, product measures and absolute continuity

practice: Measure-theoretic proofs and pathological examples

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Functional and Harmonic Analysis
decks.description: Analyze functions as vectors and transformations as operators.

outcomes.description: Prove completeness and duality properties of Banach, Hilbert and Lp spaces.
Apply Hahn-Banach, uniform boundedness and open-mapping theorems.
Derive spectral results for compact self-adjoint operators.
Establish Fourier inversion, Plancherel and convolution results in standard settings.
Calculate distributional derivatives and use Sobolev weak-derivative norms.

includes: Linear functional analysis, Fourier theory and distribution foundations

practice: Operator proofs and Fourier-distribution calculations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Differential Geometry
decks.description: Calculate intrinsic geometric quantities on smooth manifolds.

outcomes.description: Construct charts, tangent spaces, vector fields and tensor transformations.
Compute exterior derivatives and integrate forms using manifold Stokes theorem.
Calculate covariant derivatives, geodesics and parallel transport.
Compute Riemannian curvature and relate it to local geometry.

includes: Smooth manifolds, tensors, forms and Riemannian geometry

practice: Coordinate calculations and coordinate-free proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Graduate Algebra
decks.description: Develop structural machinery connecting algebraic theories.

outcomes.description: Classify finitely generated PID modules and calculate tensor products.
Prove Galois correspondence and determine solvability of polynomial examples.
Decompose finite-group representations using characters and Maschke's theorem.
Construct exact sequences and compute elementary Hom, Ext and Tor examples.

includes: Modules, field symmetry, representations and homological foundations

practice: Structural proofs and explicit algebraic computations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Algebraic Topology
decks.description: Detect topological structure through algebraic invariants.

outcomes.description: Compute fundamental groups using homotopy and van Kampen's theorem.
Classify connected coverings through subgroup correspondence.
Construct chain complexes and calculate homology using exact sequences.
Compute elementary cohomology rings and interpret duality on manifolds.

includes: Homotopy entry, coverings, homology and cohomology

practice: Invariant calculations and topological non-equivalence proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Classical Algebraic Geometry
decks.description: Translate polynomial geometry into commutative algebra.

outcomes.description: Construct affine varieties, morphisms and coordinate rings.
Prove and apply Noetherianity and Nullstellensatz correspondence.
Use localization, dimension and tangent spaces to diagnose singularities.
Analyze projective varieties and basic intersection examples.

includes: Classical affine and projective geometry; required commutative algebra taught explicitly

practice: Polynomial computations and geometric-algebraic proofs

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Stochastic Processes
decks.description: Develop probabilistic models evolving through time.

outcomes.description: Analyze discrete and continuous-time Markov chains and Poisson processes.
Construct conditional expectations and prove elementary martingale convergence results.
Derive Brownian motion properties and distinguish pathwise from mean-square behavior.
Apply Ito calculus and solve elementary stochastic differential equations.

includes: Measure-based process theory and introductory stochastic calculus

practice: Process proofs, simulation and stochastic-model comparison

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Partial Differential Equations
decks.description: Analyze field equations and the conditions making them solvable.

outcomes.description: Classify elliptic, parabolic and hyperbolic equations and boundary data.
Construct characteristic, separation-of-variables and Green-function solutions.
Formulate weak problems and establish basic variational existence results.
Prove energy and maximum-principle estimates; diagnose ill-posed problems.

includes: Linear PDE foundations with selected nonlinear failure examples

practice: Existence proofs, boundary-value calculations and weak formulations

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Mathematical Statistics
decks.description: Derive inferential guarantees and decision principles.

outcomes.description: Derive sufficient statistics and Rao-Blackwell improvements.
Prove testing and estimation optimality under explicit loss criteria.
Derive consistency and asymptotic normality under regularity conditions.
Construct posterior decisions and assess prior sensitivity and calibration.

includes: Likelihood theory, asymptotic inference and Bayesian decision foundations

practice: Inferential proofs and simulation-based coverage studies

decks.subject: mathematics
decks.title: Advanced Combinatorics
decks.description: Prove enumeration, extremal and existence results.

outcomes.description: Extract enumeration and asymptotic information from generating functions.
Prove representative extremal graph and Ramsey bounds.
Use first-moment, second-moment and local-lemma existence arguments.
Relate graph spectra to expansion, connectivity and counting.

includes: Enumerative, extremal, probabilistic and spectral methods

practice: Extended combinatorial proofs and experimental conjecture testing

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Foundations
decks.description: Construct, execute and debug small programs.

outcomes.description: Write programs using expressions, selection, iteration and functions.
Represent structured data and read, validate and transform files.
Decompose problems using interfaces, recursion and reusable modules.
Trace execution and isolate defects with tests and debugging tools.

includes: Programming notation, basic arithmetic, execution and data handling taught from scratch

practice: Implement and test progressively larger programs

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Data Structures and Algorithms
decks.description: Design correct, efficient computational solutions.

outcomes.description: Implement and select lists, trees, heaps and hash tables.
Derive worst-case, amortized and elementary randomized cost bounds.
Prove algorithm correctness using invariants and induction.
Construct greedy, divide-and-conquer and dynamic-programming solutions.
Implement traversal, shortest-path, spanning-tree and flow algorithms.

includes: Core data structures, algorithm paradigms and proof-based analysis

practice: Programming assignments with correctness proofs and benchmarks

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Organization
decks.description: Connect digital representation to processor execution.

outcomes.description: Construct combinational and sequential circuits from Boolean logic.
Calculate binary, signed-integer and floating-point representations and errors.
Trace instruction execution through assembly, datapaths and control.
Analyze caches, pipelines, vector units and hardware parallelism.

includes: Digital logic through processor and memory architecture

practice: Logic simulation, assembly programs and architecture measurements

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Systems Programming and Operating Systems
decks.description: Program and explain local machine resource management.

outcomes.description: Write pointer-based programs and diagnose lifetime and memory-safety failures.
Use command-line tools, linking and system-call interfaces.
Explain process isolation, scheduling and interprocess communication.
Trace address translation, paging and memory-allocation policies.
Implement synchronization and diagnose races, deadlock and starvation.
Explain file-system organization, persistence and crash recovery.

includes: Low-level programming taught explicitly; operating-system abstractions and implementation

practice: Build systems programs and small operating-system components

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Networks
decks.description: Explain and implement communication across layered networks.

outcomes.description: Trace packets through link, network, transport and application layers.
Calculate addressing and routing behavior under topology changes.
Analyze reliable delivery, flow control and congestion control.
Implement socket applications and diagnose naming, latency and protocol failures.

includes: Layered protocols, routing, transport and application networking

practice: Packet analysis and isolated network programming labs

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Databases and Information Retrieval
decks.description: Organize, query and retrieve persistent information.

outcomes.description: Design relational schemas using keys, dependencies and normalization.
Express and verify queries in relational algebra and SQL.
Compare indexes, join algorithms and query execution plans.
Analyze serializability, isolation anomalies and recovery protocols.
Build inverted indexes and evaluate ranked retrieval using relevance metrics.

includes: Relational data management, transaction theory and textual retrieval

practice: Build a transactional application and a small search engine

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Software Engineering
decks.description: Develop maintainable software through disciplined collaboration.

outcomes.description: Elicit requirements and translate them into testable acceptance criteria.
Design modular architectures and justify interface and dependency decisions.
Construct unit, integration and property-based testing strategies.
Use version control, review, continuous integration and safe refactoring.

includes: Requirements through collaborative maintenance and deployment principles

practice: Team project with issue tracking, reviews and releases

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Languages and Computation
decks.description: Characterize what computation can express and decide.

outcomes.description: Construct finite automata and prove regular-language closure and limitations.
Relate context-free grammars, parsing and pushdown automata.
Prove undecidability using Turing machines, simulation and reductions.
Distinguish P and NP and prove representative NP-completeness results.

includes: Automata, language hierarchies, computability and introductory complexity

practice: Machine constructions and reduction proofs

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Programming Language Theory
decks.description: Explain program meaning and language-level guarantees.

outcomes.description: Define operational semantics and reason about observational equivalence.
Derive typing judgments and prove progress and preservation for small languages.
Evaluate lambda calculus, polymorphism and algebraic data abstractions.
Compare mutation, ownership, garbage collection and effect disciplines.

includes: Formal semantics, type systems and language abstraction mechanisms

practice: Implement interpreters and prove small-language properties

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Compiler Construction
decks.description: Translate source programs into efficient executable representations.

outcomes.description: Implement lexical analysis, parsing, name resolution and type checking.
Construct control-flow and static-single-assignment intermediate representations.
Implement dataflow optimizations and justify their semantic preconditions.
Generate code with instruction selection, calling conventions and register allocation.

includes: End-to-end compiler construction and transformation correctness

practice: Build and test a compiler for a small language

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Security
decks.description: Model threats and validate layered defenses.

outcomes.description: Construct threat models distinguishing assets, adversaries and trust boundaries.
Explain memory, access-control and application failures and implement mitigations.
Apply encryption, authentication and key management without inventing primitives.
Design authorized security tests, monitoring and incident-response evidence collection.

includes: Defensive systems, application and network security; cryptographic use

practice: Contained vulnerable-system labs and defensive design reviews

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Symbolic Artificial Intelligence
decks.description: Build agents that search, reason and plan.

outcomes.description: Implement informed and adversarial search and prove relevant guarantees.
Solve constraint-satisfaction problems using propagation and search.
Represent knowledge logically and perform sound inference.
Construct plans with explicit action preconditions, effects and costs.

includes: Symbolic search, knowledge representation and planning

practice: Build puzzle-solving and planning agents

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Machine Learning
decks.description: Fit and evaluate predictive representations from data.

outcomes.description: Derive and fit regularized linear, probabilistic and tree-based predictors.
Apply clustering and dimensionality reduction with appropriate diagnostics.
Derive backpropagation and train neural networks using gradient optimization.
Assess generalization, leakage, imbalance, calibration and distribution shift.

includes: Statistical learning foundations; gradient optimization taught computationally

practice: Reproducible prediction projects with held-out evaluation

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Human-Computer Interaction
decks.description: Design and evaluate technology around human capabilities.

outcomes.description: Investigate user goals using interviews, observation and task analysis.
Apply perception, memory and action models to interface design.
Conduct usability studies and distinguish qualitative from quantitative evidence.
Design accessible interactions and assess exclusion, privacy and ethical tradeoffs.

includes: Human-factors foundations, prototyping and user-centered evaluation

practice: Iterative prototypes and consent-based usability studies

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Graphics
decks.description: Synthesize images and motion from geometric scene models.

outcomes.description: Represent meshes and apply homogeneous transforms and camera projections.
Implement visibility, clipping, interpolation and texture sampling.
Derive basic rendering equations and implement Monte Carlo light transport.
Construct interpolated, articulated and physically based animation.

includes: Geometric modeling, image synthesis and animation; sampling theory introduced

practice: Build a renderer and animated scene

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Distributed and Parallel Computing
decks.description: Reason about computation under concurrency, communication and failure.

outcomes.description: Formalize asynchronous execution, causality and failure assumptions.
Prove consensus safety and explain liveness and impossibility boundaries.
Compare linearizability, causal consistency and transactional replication.
Design shared-memory, message-passing and accelerator algorithms using work-span analysis.
Build fault-tolerant services and test recovery, partition and overload behavior.

includes: Distributed correctness, replication and parallel performance models

practice: Implement replicated services and parallel kernels; inject controlled faults

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Modern Cryptography
decks.description: Construct and justify cryptographic security guarantees.

outcomes.description: Formulate adversarial security games and prove reductions.
Derive encryption and authentication constructions from pseudorandom primitives.
Analyze public-key encryption and signatures under stated hardness assumptions.
Construct elementary commitments and zero-knowledge protocols with security arguments.

includes: Provable cryptography and protocol foundations

practice: Reduction proofs and toy implementations with attack tests

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Formal Verification
decks.description: Establish machine-checked guarantees for finite and symbolic systems.

outcomes.description: Prove program contracts using Hoare logic and loop invariants.
Specify temporal properties and verify finite-state models.
Encode verification conditions in SAT and SMT and interpret counterexamples.
Prove abstraction and refinement relations between system models.

includes: Deductive verification, temporal model checking and solver-based methods

practice: Verify programs and protocols with explicit trusted assumptions

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Machine Learning
decks.description: Develop probabilistic, generative and sequential learning theory.

outcomes.description: Derive exact and approximate inference in probabilistic graphical models.
Derive variational and diffusion objectives and evaluate generative models.
Derive dynamic-programming, value-learning and policy-gradient methods.
Prove representative generalization bounds and analyze optimization-generalization tradeoffs.

includes: Probabilistic modeling, deep generative methods, reinforcement learning and learning theory

practice: Derive objectives and reproduce controlled research-scale experiments

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Computer Vision
decks.description: Infer scene structure and meaning from images.

outcomes.description: Model image formation, filtering, sampling and sensor noise.
Estimate camera geometry, motion and three-dimensional structure.
Train and evaluate detection, segmentation and recognition systems.
Formulate regularized inverse-imaging problems and analyze ambiguity.

includes: Classical image processing, multiview geometry and learned visual inference

practice: Calibrated image experiments and reproducible vision pipelines

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Advanced Computational Complexity
decks.description: Analyze resource limits beyond elementary tractability.

outcomes.description: Prove representative time and space hierarchy results.
Analyze randomized classes, amplification and derandomization assumptions.
Establish counting hardness and compare decision and counting reductions.
Prove elementary circuit lower bounds and explain proof barriers.

includes: Time, space, randomness, counting and circuit complexity

practice: Reduction, diagonalization and lower-bound proofs

decks.subject: computer-science
decks.title: Robotics
decks.description: Integrate embodied estimation, feedback and planning.

outcomes.description: Derive rigid-body transformations, manipulator kinematics and simple robot dynamics.
Implement Bayesian filtering and analyze localization observability.
Design feedback controllers and establish local closed-loop stability.
Plan collision-free motion and evaluate uncertainty-aware execution.

includes: Rigid-motion notation, estimation, control and motion planning taught explicitly

practice: Simulation-first robot integration and controlled hardware experiments

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Measurement and Modeling
decks.description: Connect measurements, units and explanatory models.

outcomes.description: Check dimensional consistency and estimate physical scales.
Report measurement uncertainty and propagate independent small errors.
Construct graphs and distinguish model assumptions from measured quantities.
Design controlled measurements with calibration and reproducible records.

includes: Units, uncertainty, scaling and elementary experimental reasoning

practice: Low-risk measurements and laboratory notebooks

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Newtonian Mechanics
decks.description: Predict motion through forces and conservation laws.

outcomes.description: Solve constant-acceleration and circular-motion problems using vectors.
Construct free-body diagrams and solve Newtonian force-balance problems.
Apply work-energy and momentum conservation to collisions and gravitation.
Calculate torque, angular momentum and elementary rigid-body motion.

includes: Algebra-based mechanics; vector components introduced locally

practice: Mechanics problem sets and motion-tracking experiments

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Waves and Optics
decks.description: Predict wave propagation and optical image formation.

outcomes.description: Model sinusoidal oscillations, traveling waves and wave energy.
Calculate beats, standing waves, resonance and Doppler shifts.
Construct images using reflection, refraction, lenses and optical instruments.
Calculate elementary interference, diffraction and polarization effects.

includes: Algebraic wave models, acoustics, geometrical and wave optics

practice: Optical bench, wave-tank or simulation investigations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Electricity, Magnetism and Circuits
decks.description: Analyze elementary electromagnetic systems without field calculus.

outcomes.description: Calculate point-charge fields, potentials and electrostatic energies.
Solve resistive networks and explain capacitor and inductor transients.
Calculate magnetic forces and fields for elementary symmetric sources.
Apply magnetic-flux and induction laws with consistent signs.

includes: Algebra-based fields, circuit laws and induction; vector products introduced

practice: Low-voltage circuit measurements and field calculations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Heat and Thermodynamics
decks.description: Reason about energy transfer and irreversible change.

outcomes.description: Relate temperature, heat transfer, ideal gases and phase changes.
Calculate heat, work and internal-energy changes with stated conventions.
Calculate elementary entropy changes and identify irreversible processes.
Analyze heat engines, refrigerators and thermodynamic efficiency limits.

includes: Algebraic macroscopic thermodynamics and elementary entropy

practice: Calorimetry, cycle diagrams and energy-budget problems

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Modern Physics: First Models
decks.description: Explain experiments that require relativistic or quantum ideas.

outcomes.description: Calculate Lorentz kinematics, time dilation and relativistic energy-momentum.
Explain blackbody and photoelectric evidence and calculate photon processes.
Apply de Broglie relations, uncertainty and elementary atomic energy models.
Calculate binding energies and radioactive decay; distinguish nuclear processes.

includes: Algebra-based modern-physics phenomena and model limitations

practice: Experimental-data interpretation and order-of-magnitude calculations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Analytical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive classical dynamics using variational and phase-space methods.

outcomes.description: Derive Euler-Lagrange equations and conservation laws from symmetries.
Use Hamilton equations, Poisson brackets and canonical transformations.
Derive normal modes and analyze coupled small oscillations.
Solve central-force and rigid-body problems with stability analysis.

includes: Calculus of variations taught explicitly; Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics

practice: Extended derivations and numerical trajectory comparisons

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Classical Electrodynamics
decks.description: Solve electromagnetic field equations and radiation problems.

outcomes.description: Derive field conservation laws from differential Maxwell equations.
Solve electrostatic boundary problems using separation, multipoles and Green functions.
Derive wave propagation, reflection and dispersion in material media.
Calculate retarded potentials and nonrelativistic dipole radiation.

includes: Maxwell theory; Fourier expansion, separation and Green methods taught computationally

practice: Boundary-value derivations and field simulations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Mechanics
decks.description: Calculate quantum states, measurements and elementary dynamics.

outcomes.description: Apply state-vector, operator and measurement postulates with probability amplitudes.
Solve standard one-dimensional potentials and use position-momentum Fourier representations.
Calculate spin, angular momentum and hydrogenic states.
Apply variational and perturbative methods with validity checks.
Construct bosonic and fermionic states and explain exchange effects.

includes: Hilbert-space notation introduced explicitly; elementary wave mechanics and approximations

practice: Analytical wavefunction problems and numerical eigenvalue studies

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Statistical Mechanics
decks.description: Derive macroscopic behavior from microscopic statistical models.

outcomes.description: Derive microcanonical, canonical and grand-canonical distributions and thermodynamic observables.
Calculate classical, Bose and Fermi ideal-gas behavior.
Analyze order parameters, mean-field transitions and critical scaling.
Relate fluctuations, response and elementary transport to microscopic statistics.

includes: Equilibrium ensembles, quantum occupation statistics and introductory nonequilibrium response

practice: Partition-function derivations and model simulations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Fluid and Elastic Continua
decks.description: Model continuous matter with balance and constitutive laws.

outcomes.description: Derive mass, momentum and energy balances using stress tensors.
Solve elementary linear-elastic deformation and wave problems.
Derive Navier-Stokes equations and solve canonical viscous flows.
Use dimensionless groups to analyze boundary layers and instability onset.

includes: Tensor-component notation, continuum conservation, elasticity and fluid mechanics

practice: Flow and deformation calculations with dimensional experiments

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Experimental Physics Methods
decks.description: Build measurement chains and infer physical parameters.

outcomes.description: Design amplifier, filter and sensor readout circuits using basic device models.
Analyze sampled signals using Fourier spectra and noise models.
Construct calibration and systematic-uncertainty budgets for instruments.
Fit competing physical models and report reproducible uncertainty-qualified results.

includes: Electronics, sampling and Fourier methods taught for instrumentation

practice: Instrument-building and open-ended measurement projects

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Computational Physics
decks.description: Build and validate numerical models of physical systems.

outcomes.description: Implement symplectic molecular and particle dynamics with conservation diagnostics.
Implement Monte Carlo sampling and estimate autocorrelation-adjusted uncertainty.
Discretize representative diffusion and Poisson equations and test stability.
Separate finite-size, discretization, sampling and model errors.

includes: Particle, lattice and field simulation; finite-difference foundations taught explicitly

practice: Reproducible simulation studies with benchmark limits

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Relativity and Gravitation
decks.description: Develop covariant mechanics and curved-spacetime gravitation.

outcomes.description: Derive Lorentz-covariant mechanics using four-vectors and tensors.
Calculate geodesic motion and geodesic deviation in spacetime metrics.
Derive Einstein equations from geometric and variational principles.
Analyze Schwarzschild, weak-field and gravitational-wave solutions and their limits.

includes: Covariant special relativity, Lorentzian geometry and general relativity

practice: Tensor derivations and spacetime trajectory calculations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Graduate Quantum Theory
decks.description: Extend quantum mechanics to symmetry, scattering and open dynamics.

outcomes.description: Use unitary symmetries and angular-momentum addition to constrain quantum systems.
Derive scattering amplitudes using partial waves and approximation methods.
Calculate mixed states, entanglement and reduced-system observables.
Derive time-dependent transitions and elementary open-system master equations.

includes: Advanced nonrelativistic quantum formalism and density-operator dynamics

practice: Scattering derivations and open-system simulations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Condensed Matter Physics
decks.description: Explain material properties through structure and collective excitations.

outcomes.description: Calculate reciprocal lattices, diffraction conditions and phonon spectra.
Derive elementary electronic bands and distinguish metals, semiconductors and insulators.
Calculate elementary electrical and thermal transport with scattering models.
Explain magnetic order and superconductivity using microscopic and phenomenological models.

includes: Crystalline structure, excitations, electronic properties and ordered phases

practice: Band, lattice and transport calculations with data comparison

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Many-Body Physics
decks.description: Analyze interacting quantum matter and emergent phases.

outcomes.description: Construct second-quantized models and derive elementary quasiparticle descriptions.
Calculate Green functions and linear response using controlled approximations.
Analyze broken symmetry, collective modes and elementary renormalization flows.
Calculate Berry phases and basic topological band invariants.

includes: Many-body operators, response, criticality and topological quantum matter

practice: Model derivations and numerical phase diagnostics

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Nuclear and Particle Physics
decks.description: Connect subatomic structure to reactions and experimental evidence.

outcomes.description: Compare liquid-drop, shell and collective nuclear models quantitatively.
Calculate decay kinematics, cross sections and reaction thresholds.
Use Standard Model quantum numbers and symmetries to classify interactions.
Infer particle properties from detector signatures and conservation constraints.

includes: Nuclear structure, reaction phenomenology and particle classification

practice: Nuclear calculations and public detector-data analysis

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Atomic, Molecular and Optical Physics
decks.description: Analyze microscopic structure and controlled light-matter dynamics.

outcomes.description: Calculate atomic fine structure and molecular rotational-vibrational spectra.
Derive transition strengths and selection rules from symmetry.
Solve driven few-level dynamics and explain laser gain and cooling.
Calculate coherence and photon correlations using quantized optical modes.

includes: Atomic and molecular structure, spectroscopy, lasers and quantum optics

practice: Spectroscopic derivations and driven-system simulations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Astrophysics
decks.description: Infer the structure and evolution of astronomical systems.

outcomes.description: Infer luminosity, distance, temperature and motion from astronomical observations.
Derive stellar structure balances and explain stellar evolution.
Estimate degeneracy-supported remnant limits and accretion energy scales.
Analyze galactic dynamics, interstellar matter and dark-matter evidence.

includes: Radiative transfer introduced; stellar, interstellar and galactic astrophysics

practice: Public observation analysis and stellar-model calculations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Plasma Physics
decks.description: Analyze collective dynamics of charged matter.

outcomes.description: Calculate charged-particle drifts, confinement and plasma screening scales.
Derive kinetic descriptions and analyze elementary Landau damping.
Derive plasma-fluid and magnetohydrodynamic models and wave modes.
Analyze representative plasma instabilities and model-validity limits.

includes: Particle, kinetic and fluid plasma descriptions

practice: Dispersion derivations and plasma-model simulations

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Physical Cosmology
decks.description: Model cosmic evolution and confront it with observations.

outcomes.description: Derive Friedmann evolution and calculate cosmological distances.
Calculate equilibrium departure, nucleosynthesis and recombination scales.
Derive linear structure growth and interpret primordial fluctuation spectra.
Compare cosmological models using expansion, microwave-background and structure evidence.

includes: Relativistic cosmology, thermal history, linear perturbations and parameter inference

practice: Background solvers and public cosmological likelihood exercises

decks.subject: physics
decks.title: Quantum Field Theory
decks.description: Calculate relativistic quantum interactions within effective theories.

outcomes.description: Quantize scalar, spinor and gauge fields using canonical and path-integral methods.
Derive diagrammatic rules and calculate elementary scattering amplitudes.
Regularize loop integrals and derive elementary renormalization-group running.
Derive gauge interactions and explain symmetry breaking in Standard Model sectors.

includes: Relativistic field notation and perturbative quantum field foundations

practice: Extended amplitude and renormalization calculations

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Foundations
decks.description: Connect particulate models, chemical symbols and measured amounts.

outcomes.description: Interpret atomic, ionic and isotopic notation and periodic organization.
Construct Lewis structures and predict elementary geometry and intermolecular forces.
Balance reactions and calculate limiting reagents, yields and composition.
Prepare concentration calculations and explain dissolution and solution properties.

includes: Chemical representations, bonding models, mole arithmetic and solutions

practice: Stoichiometric problems and supervised basic preparation exercises

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Equilibria
decks.description: Predict chemical composition and electrochemical driving forces.

outcomes.description: Solve mass-action and balance equations and assess approximation validity.
Calculate pH, buffers and polyprotic titration behavior.
Predict precipitation and complexation under competing equilibria.
Balance redox reactions and calculate cell potentials with the Nernst equation.

includes: Computational equilibria, acid-base, solubility, complexation and electrochemical cells

practice: Equilibrium calculations and supervised titration or cell experiments

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organic Structure and Reactivity
decks.description: Explain carbon chemistry through structure and electron movement.

outcomes.description: Use resonance, acidity and conformational analysis to compare organic structures.
Assign stereochemistry and predict stereoisomeric relationships and reaction outcomes.
Construct substitution, elimination, addition and carbonyl electron-pushing mechanisms.
Select functional-group transformations and plan short syntheses.

includes: Organic representation grammar, stereochemistry and core functional-group mechanisms

practice: Mechanism problems, model building and supervised synthesis labs

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Inorganic Chemistry
decks.description: Explain elemental and coordination chemistry through bonding trends.

outcomes.description: Explain periodic trends using shielding, oxidation state and bonding models.
Predict representative main-group structures, reactions and anomalous trends.
Relate complex geometry, ligand fields, spin and magnetic behavior.
Assign molecular point groups and use symmetry to classify vibrations.

includes: Descriptive and explanatory main-group and coordination chemistry; symmetry notation

practice: Structure prediction and supervised inorganic preparation or characterization

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Analysis and Structure Determination
decks.description: Infer chemical amounts and identities from measurements.

outcomes.description: Design sampling, calibration and validation with detection-limit and uncertainty estimates.
Select and calculate titrimetric, gravimetric and potentiometric determinations.
Explain chromatographic retention, resolution and method-selection tradeoffs.
Interpret absorption and infrared spectra and calculate quantitative absorbance.
Infer elementary molecular connectivity and stereochemical constraints from NMR spectra.
Infer formulas and structural fragments from mass spectra.

includes: Quantitative analytical methods, separations and introductory spectroscopic interpretation

practice: Unknown identification and validated quantitative analysis projects

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Kinetics
decks.description: Connect reaction rates to mechanisms and experimental evidence.

outcomes.description: Determine rate laws and integrate elementary reaction kinetics.
Derive rate expressions using pre-equilibrium and steady-state approximations.
Interpret Arrhenius and transition-state parameters and their limitations.
Analyze catalytic and enzyme cycles including inhibition and saturation.

includes: Reaction-rate theory, mechanistic approximations and elementary catalysis

practice: Fit kinetic data and discriminate competing mechanisms

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Chemical Thermodynamics
decks.description: Derive chemical equilibrium from energy and entropy.

outcomes.description: Derive thermodynamic potentials, Maxwell relations and chemical potentials.
Calculate activities and partial molar properties of nonideal mixtures.
Construct phase diagrams and apply phase-rule and coexistence conditions.
Derive reaction and electrochemical equilibrium from Gibbs-energy minimization.

includes: Differential thermodynamics, mixtures, phases and reaction equilibrium

practice: Thermodynamic derivations and experimental phase-data analysis

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Biochemistry
decks.description: Explain biological function through molecular chemistry and energy flow.

outcomes.description: Relate protein, nucleic-acid, carbohydrate and lipid structures to function.
Explain catalytic strategies and interpret enzyme regulation and inhibition.
Trace central catabolic flux and identify metabolic control points.
Calculate energetic coupling in chemiosmosis, respiration and photosynthesis.
Trace major anabolic pathways and explain their coordination with catabolism.

includes: Macromolecular chemistry, enzyme mechanisms and integrated metabolism

practice: Pathway perturbation problems and enzyme-data analysis

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Quantum Chemistry
decks.description: Derive molecular bonding and spectra from quantum models.

outcomes.description: Apply Born-Oppenheimer and antisymmetry approximations to molecular electronic structure.
Construct molecular orbitals and compare valence-bond and orbital descriptions.
Use character tables and symmetry-adapted combinations in molecular calculations.
Derive rotational, vibrational and electronic spectral structures and selection rules.

includes: Molecular quantum theory and spectroscopic foundations; representation tools taught locally

practice: Molecular orbital derivations and spectral calculations

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Organometallic Chemistry and Catalysis
decks.description: Connect metal-ligand bonding to catalytic transformations.

outcomes.description: Use electron counting and orbital models to assess metal-complex bonding.
Explain ligand substitution, oxidative addition, insertion and elimination mechanisms.
Construct catalytic cycles and derive kinetic and thermodynamic constraints.
Predict ligand and metal effects on catalytic activity and selectivity.

includes: Advanced coordination reactivity and homogeneous catalysis

practice: Catalytic-cycle analysis and literature-based catalyst comparison

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Solid-State and Materials Chemistry
decks.description: Relate chemical preparation and defects to material function.

outcomes.description: Determine crystal structures and interpret diffraction patterns.
Calculate defect equilibria and explain nonstoichiometry and diffusion.
Relate chemical bonding and microstructure to electronic, ionic and mechanical behavior.
Design synthesis and characterization routes controlling phase and microstructure.

includes: Crystallographic notation, defect chemistry and structure-property design

practice: Structure refinement exercises and supervised materials preparation

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Polymer Chemistry
decks.description: Connect macromolecular synthesis, statistics and bulk behavior.

outcomes.description: Derive step-growth and chain-growth kinetics and predict architecture.
Calculate molecular-mass averages and interpret dispersity measurements.
Derive ideal-chain statistics and explain solvent and excluded-volume effects.
Relate chain structure to glass transition, crystallinity and viscoelastic response.

includes: Polymer synthesis, chain statistics and introductory polymer physics

practice: Polymerization calculations and molecular-mass or rheology analysis

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Environmental Chemistry
decks.description: Explain chemical fate across coupled environmental compartments.

outcomes.description: Predict aqueous and soil speciation, sorption and redox transformations.
Construct compartment mass balances for chemical transport and degradation.
Analyze atmospheric radical chemistry, ozone and pollutant formation.
Design chemical monitoring and evaluate exposure and remediation evidence.

includes: Atmospheric, aquatic and terrestrial chemical processes

practice: Environmental datasets, mass-balance models and sampling plans

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Medicinal Chemistry and Chemical Biology
decks.description: Design molecular interventions and interpret target engagement.

outcomes.description: Evaluate target validation, binding assays and mechanism-of-action evidence.
Develop structure-activity hypotheses balancing potency, selectivity and physicochemical properties.
Calculate elementary pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic models and identify exposure limits.
Design chemical probes with controls for localization and off-target effects.
Explain reactive-metabolite, off-target and dose-dependent toxicity mechanisms.

includes: Drug and probe design, ADME, target engagement and chemical toxicology

practice: Assay critique and evidence-based molecular design projects

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Nuclear and Radiochemistry
decks.description: Use nuclear transformations as chemical probes and separation targets.

outcomes.description: Calculate coupled decay, activation and isotope production balances.
Explain radiochemical separations and isotope-dependent chemical behavior.
Design isotope-tracer balances and distinguish tracer from perturbation effects.
Interpret counting statistics, detector efficiency and radiation-dose quantities.

includes: Decay chemistry, isotope tracers, separations and radiation measurement

practice: Simulated tracer studies and public radiation datasets

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Advanced Organic Synthesis and Mechanism
decks.description: Design selective syntheses supported by mechanistic evidence.

outcomes.description: Use kinetic isotope effects and linear free-energy relationships to discriminate mechanisms.
Derive pericyclic and photochemical selection predictions using orbital symmetry.
Construct strategic disconnections for complex molecular targets.
Design chemo-, regio- and stereoselective transformations including asymmetric catalysis.
Compare complete synthetic routes for feasibility, verification and material efficiency.

includes: Physical organic evidence, orbital control and advanced synthesis design

practice: Multistep synthesis proposals and critical mechanism dossiers

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Surface and Electrochemical Interfaces
decks.description: Explain reactions and organization at material boundaries.

outcomes.description: Derive surface-energy and adsorption relations and interpret adsorption isotherms.
Compare electrical double-layer models and calculate interfacial capacitance.
Derive electrode kinetic and diffusion responses in voltammetry.
Analyze heterogeneous catalytic mechanisms and distinguish kinetic from transport control.
Predict colloidal stability using interparticle forces and interfacial thermodynamics.

includes: Surface thermodynamics, electrochemical kinetics, heterogeneous catalysis and colloids

practice: Voltammetry, adsorption and catalytic-rate model analysis

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Computational Chemistry
decks.description: Calculate molecular properties with explicit approximation control.

outcomes.description: Derive Hartree-Fock and Kohn-Sham working principles and compare correlation approximations.
Locate minima and transition states and validate reaction pathways.
Construct molecular partition functions and calculate statistical thermochemical corrections.
Implement or configure molecular dynamics and free-energy sampling methods.
Quantify basis, functional, force-field, sampling and finite-size limitations.

includes: Electronic structure, molecular statistical thermochemistry and simulation

practice: Benchmarked molecular calculations with reproducible input and analysis

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Photochemistry
decks.description: Explain chemical transformations on excited-state landscapes.

outcomes.description: Construct excited-state diagrams and distinguish radiative and nonradiative transitions.
Derive quantum yields, lifetimes and quenching relationships.
Explain photochemical pathways using excited surfaces and conical-intersection concepts.
Interpret time-resolved spectra and design mechanism-discriminating controls.

includes: Excited-state energetics, kinetics and experimental mechanistic interpretation

practice: Transient-data analysis and photochemical mechanism comparisons

decks.subject: chemistry
decks.title: Supramolecular Chemistry
decks.description: Design chemical function through reversible molecular organization.

outcomes.description: Analyze host-guest binding using geometry, solvation and thermodynamics.
Derive multivalent and cooperative binding models and fit binding data.
Distinguish equilibrium assembly, kinetic trapping and dissipative organization.
Design molecular assemblies and propose orthogonal structural and functional tests.

includes: Molecular recognition, cooperative binding and self-assembly
excludes: Complete theory of active soft matter

practice: Binding-model analysis and literature-grounded assembly design

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Biological Foundations
decks.description: Explain living systems across organization, inheritance and evidence.

outcomes.description: Relate cells, organisms and ecosystems using energy, information and homeostasis.
Explain qualitative roles of water, membranes and major biological molecules.
Explain inherited variation, selection and common ancestry without teleology.
Interpret biological diagrams and distinguish observation, hypothesis, experiment and inference.

includes: Biological representation grammar and qualitative physical-chemical ideas taught locally

practice: Observation journals and evidence-based explanations

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Cell and Molecular Biology
decks.description: Explain cellular organization and biological information flow.

outcomes.description: Relate organelles, cytoskeleton and membrane trafficking to cellular functions.
Predict membrane transport from gradients, permeability and transporter properties.
Explain DNA replication, repair and mutation mechanisms.
Explain transcription, RNA processing, translation and elementary gene regulation.
Trace receptor signaling and feedback from extracellular cues to responses.
Explain cell-cycle regulation, mitosis, meiosis and programmed cell death.

includes: Mechanistic cell organization, genome maintenance and expression

practice: Microscopy interpretation and molecular perturbation reasoning

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Transmission Genetics
decks.description: Infer inheritance mechanisms from crosses and families.

outcomes.description: Predict Mendelian and non-Mendelian crosses using chromosome segregation.
Estimate recombination and construct genetic linkage maps.
Infer inheritance models while accounting for penetrance and ascertainment.
Distinguish chromosomal, allelic and environmental causes of phenotypic variation.

includes: Chromosome and meiosis concepts taught locally; crosses, linkage and pedigrees

practice: Cross analysis, pedigree problems and simulated inheritance

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolution and Organismal Diversity
decks.description: Explain biological diversity through common ancestry and adaptation.

outcomes.description: Distinguish selection, drift, mutation and gene flow using biological evidence.
Compare species concepts and explain reproductive isolation and speciation.
Read and construct elementary phylogenies and distinguish homology from convergence.
Compare bacterial, archaeal and major protist organization and life histories.
Compare major plant and fungal structures, innovations and reproductive cycles.
Compare animal body plans, organ-system innovations and developmental patterns.

includes: Evolutionary evidence, fossil reasoning and comparative major-lineage biology

practice: Comparative specimen or image analysis and phylogenetic arguments

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Ecology
decks.description: Explain organism-environment relationships across ecological scales.

outcomes.description: Calculate elementary population growth and life-table quantities.
Explain competition, predation, mutualism and community assembly using evidence.
Construct energy and nutrient budgets for terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems.
Design ecological sampling and distinguish scale, detection and replication effects.

includes: Algebraic population models, communities, ecosystems and field inference

practice: Field or public-data studies and ecosystem budget calculations

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Microbiology
decks.description: Explain microbial physiology, replication and experimental study.

outcomes.description: Calculate microbial growth and explain environmental control of populations.
Compare microbial energy strategies and their ecological consequences.
Explain horizontal gene transfer and mobile genetic elements.
Compare viral genome strategies, replication cycles and host dependence.
Design culture, identification and contamination-control workflows for appropriate organisms.

includes: Bacterial, archaeal and eukaryotic microbial physiology; virology and culture principles

practice: Approved nonpathogenic culture exercises or validated virtual laboratories

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Plant Biology
decks.description: Explain how plant structure supports growth and resource acquisition.

outcomes.description: Relate plant tissues, organs and life cycles to their functions.
Explain water potential, xylem transport, stomata and phloem allocation.
Compare photosynthetic pathways and predict elementary carbon-water tradeoffs.
Explain meristem growth, hormonal regulation and environmental developmental responses.

includes: Functional anatomy, transport, photosynthesis and plant development

practice: Plant-growth experiments, anatomy and gas-exchange data interpretation

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Comparative Animal Physiology
decks.description: Explain normal organ-system function through regulated exchange.

outcomes.description: Analyze feedback, set points and comparative physiological constraints.
Explain membrane potentials, action potentials, synapses and muscle contraction.
Analyze circulation, gas exchange and renal-osmotic regulation using balances.
Explain digestion, absorption and organismal energy allocation.
Trace endocrine axes and predict feedback responses.
Explain gametogenesis, reproductive cycles and comparative reproductive regulation.

includes: Comparative organ physiology; electrical-gradient and flow models taught locally

practice: Physiological data interpretation and noninvasive model experiments

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Behavioral Biology
decks.description: Explain behavior through mechanism, development and evolutionary function.

outcomes.description: Separate proximate and ultimate hypotheses and design discriminating observations.
Distinguish learning mechanisms and developmental influences on behavior.
Analyze sensory ecology, signaling reliability and receiver responses.
Explain mating, cooperation and social conflict using fitness-based models.

includes: Ethology, learning, communication and behavioral ecology

practice: Ethograms and preregistered observational studies

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Experimental Biology
decks.description: Generate interpretable biological measurements and causal tests.

outcomes.description: Design biological experiments addressing controls, replication, randomization and power.
Choose microscopy methods and quantify images while diagnosing artifacts.
Design nucleic-acid and protein assays with calibration and contamination controls.
Design genetic or pharmacological perturbations and distinguish causation from assay artifacts.

includes: Microscopy, pipetting and assay principles, molecular measurement and causal intervention

practice: Supervised assays and complete reproducible experimental reports

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Developmental Biology
decks.description: Explain how cellular decisions construct organized organisms.

outcomes.description: Infer cell specification, determination and lineage from perturbation evidence.
Explain positional information, induction and gene-regulatory patterning.
Relate cell adhesion, migration and mechanics to tissue shaping.
Compare stem-cell regulation, regeneration and evolutionary developmental change.

includes: Animal and plant developmental mechanisms and experimental reasoning

practice: Lineage and perturbation-data analysis; developmental model comparisons

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Neuroscience
decks.description: Connect neural signaling to circuits, behavior and plasticity.

outcomes.description: Model membrane and channel dynamics using conductance-based equations.
Explain synaptic integration, modulation and excitation-inhibition balance.
Analyze representative sensory, motor and cognitive circuit computations.
Explain learning-related plasticity and representative neurological dysfunction mechanisms.
Interpret neural recordings and perturbations while distinguishing correlation from function.

includes: Cellular, systems and cognitive neuroscience with quantitative membrane models

practice: Neural-signal analysis and conductance-model simulation

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Immunology
decks.description: Explain immune recognition, defense and dysregulation.

outcomes.description: Trace barrier defense, innate recognition, inflammation and complement activation.
Explain lymphocyte activation, effector differentiation and immune memory.
Explain antigen presentation and receptor diversity and specificity.
Derive mechanisms of tolerance failure, hypersensitivity and immunodeficiency.
Evaluate vaccine and immune-assay evidence using mechanistic predictions.

includes: Innate and adaptive immunology, immune pathology and vaccination principles

practice: Immune-response case analysis and experimental-data interpretation

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Population and Quantitative Genetics
decks.description: Model genetic variation and evolutionary change quantitatively.

outcomes.description: Derive Hardy-Weinberg expectations and test departures with appropriate assumptions.
Calculate allele-frequency changes under selection, drift, mutation and migration.
Partition quantitative-trait variance and predict selection response with limitations.
Relate linkage disequilibrium and elementary coalescent genealogies to demographic history.

includes: Deterministic and stochastic population genetics; quantitative inheritance

practice: Population simulations and allele-frequency or trait-data analysis

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Conservation and Global-Change Biology
decks.description: Evaluate biodiversity risks and intervention strategies.

outcomes.description: Estimate population viability using demographic and genetic evidence.
Analyze fragmentation, connectivity and reserve-design tradeoffs.
Evaluate climate, exploitation, invasion and pollution impacts across scales.
Compare conservation actions using monitoring, uncertainty and human-context constraints.

includes: Conservation genetics, landscape ecology, global change and adaptive management

practice: Spatial conservation assessments and intervention monitoring plans

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Genomics and Bioinformatics
decks.description: Infer biological structure and variation from high-throughput data.

outcomes.description: Implement alignment and explain assembly, annotation and sequencing-error tradeoffs.
Construct variant-analysis workflows and assess mapping and ascertainment biases.
Analyze bulk and single-cell expression with normalization and multiplicity control.
Infer sequence phylogenies and diagnose model, alignment and gene-tree conflicts.

includes: Sequence algorithms, genomic variation, transcriptomics and phylogenetic inference

practice: Reproducible public-data pipelines with provenance and sensitivity analysis

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Systems Biology
decks.description: Infer and test quantitative models of biological networks.

outcomes.description: Construct biochemical network models and perform stoichiometric flux analysis.
Analyze feedback, oscillation and multistability in regulatory ODE models.
Derive chemical master equations and simulate stochastic reaction networks.
Assess parameter identifiability and design informative perturbation experiments.

includes: Network, deterministic and stochastic systems modeling with inference

practice: Model-data integration projects and prospective perturbation predictions

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Structural Biology and Molecular Biophysics
decks.description: Connect molecular ensembles to structures and biological mechanics.

outcomes.description: Derive binding and conformational models from molecular free-energy landscapes.
Infer structures from diffraction, NMR and cryo-EM while assessing resolution and ambiguity.
Analyze folding, aggregation and allostery through thermodynamic and kinetic evidence.
Model molecular motors and force spectroscopy using thermal and mechanical balances.

includes: Molecular ensembles, structural reconstruction principles, folding and mechanochemistry

practice: Structural-data critique, binding fits and single-molecule model analysis

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Evolutionary Theory
decks.description: Develop mechanistic and inferential models of evolutionary change.

outcomes.description: Derive invasion-fitness and evolutionary-game models and assess equilibrium stability.
Derive coalescent likelihood principles under demography, recombination and selection.
Fit phylogenetic comparative models and diagnose nonindependence and confounding.
Compare diversification and extinction models using fossil and phylogenetic evidence.

includes: Population, comparative and macroevolutionary theory with model criticism

practice: Evolutionary derivations and comparative-data inference projects

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Theoretical Ecology
decks.description: Analyze ecological dynamics, spatial structure and resilience.

outcomes.description: Derive coexistence and stability conditions for interacting populations.
Analyze metapopulation, dispersal and reaction-diffusion ecological models.
Relate trophic network structure to energy flow and dynamical resilience.
Fit ecological state-space models and distinguish process from observation uncertainty.

includes: Nonlinear, spatial and stochastic ecological models; finite-difference spatial methods

practice: Model proofs, simulations and ecological time-series inference

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Host-Microbe and Parasite Biology
decks.description: Explain infection, symbiosis and coevolution mechanistically.

outcomes.description: Explain microbial colonization, tissue damage and immune-evasion mechanisms.
Compare protozoan, helminth and vector-associated life cycles and host constraints.
Analyze host-pathogen tradeoffs and transmission using elementary epidemiological models.
Explain antimicrobial resistance evolution and distinguish genetic resistance from tolerance.
Evaluate microbiome functional and causal claims using ecological and experimental evidence.

includes: Advanced virology, parasitology, pathogenesis, microbiomes and transmission models

practice: Public infection-data analysis and non-operational mechanism case studies

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Cell Regulation and Molecular Pathology
decks.description: Explain regulatory decisions and their pathological breakdown.

outcomes.description: Evaluate chromatin and epigenetic mechanisms using perturbation and inheritance evidence.
Explain post-transcriptional regulation and RNA surveillance through molecular mechanisms.
Explain selective trafficking, proteostasis and organelle quality-control failures.
Analyze signaling integration controlling proliferation, differentiation and cell death.
Connect genome instability, clonal selection and microenvironment to cancer progression.

includes: Advanced molecular regulation, cellular quality control and cancer mechanisms

practice: Mechanistic literature critique and perturbation-experiment design

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Integrative Physiology and Pathophysiology
decks.description: Analyze coordinated organismal responses and multiorgan failure.

outcomes.description: Explain coupled neural, endocrine and metabolic regulation across organ systems.
Analyze physiological adaptation to exercise, temperature, hypoxia and water stress.
Derive multiorgan consequences of circulatory, respiratory, renal and metabolic failures.
Construct physiological compartment models and assess parameter identifiability.

includes: Comparative integrative physiology, mechanistic disease and quantitative compartment models

practice: Physiological model fitting and mechanistic case analysis

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Advanced Plant Physiology and Interactions
decks.description: Explain plant responses to developmental and environmental constraints.

outcomes.description: Analyze hormonal, light and circadian networks controlling plant development.
Explain molecular and hydraulic responses to drought, salinity and temperature.
Explain plant immunity and bacterial, fungal and herbivore interactions.
Model carbon-nutrient allocation and design tests of productivity tradeoffs.

includes: Plant regulatory physiology, stress, defense, symbiosis and resource allocation

practice: Plant-response datasets and controlled growth-experiment proposals

decks.subject: biology
decks.title: Synthetic Biology
decks.description: Design bounded biological functions with explicit failure analysis.

outcomes.description: Design genetic circuits and predict noise, burden and context dependence.
Compare genome-editing strategies and design specificity and phenotype-validation controls.
Analyze evolutionary stability and metabolic tradeoffs in engineered biological systems.
Construct design-build-test plans with containment, misuse and ecological-risk assessment.

includes: Biological engineering principles using nonpathogenic educational models

practice: Simulation-first circuit projects and institutionally approved low-risk experiments

scopeIssues: The algorithms entry route unnecessarily inherits single-variable calculus through mathematics/probability solely to support elementary randomized cost analysis. A repair should extract a finite-probability bridge or teach finite expectation explicitly inside computer-science/algorithms, preserving the existing randomized-analysis outcome.

The first quantitative analytical-chemistry route requires the entire organic-chemistry deck because spectroscopy and quantitative analysis share one node. Splitting quantitative analytical methods from molecular structure determination would remove an unnecessary organic-mechanism prerequisite for learners entering measurement chemistry.

The advanced number-theory specification provides an undergraduate entrance to algebraic and analytic methods but not a graduate foundation in either branch. Additional graduate algebraic-number-theory and analytic-number-theory nodes are needed before the mathematical curriculum can be considered whole-field at the requested depth.

General ergodic theory, calculus of variations and optimal-control theory are not developed as independent mathematical capabilities. Variational mechanics and elementary dynamical diagnostics do not supply these established mathematical foundations.

The physics plan lacks a sufficiently developed graduate nonequilibrium statistical-physics route: elementary response, plasma kinetics and computational sampling do not together teach general kinetic theory, transport derivations and fluctuation relations.

The biological curriculum needs a distinct advanced developmental-mechanisms continuation covering quantitative morphogenesis and gene-regulatory developmental dynamics. The present graduate cell-regulation and systems-biology outcomes do not explicitly establish that capability.

The advanced structural-biophysics outcome for structure inference bundles diffraction, NMR and cryo-EM too broadly. It should be split into independently assessable reconstruction and validation outcomes, with Fourier and inverse-problem preparation made explicit.

Several mathematical and physical exclusions identify established extensions without corresponding coverage dispositions, notably ergodic theory, nonlinear PDE regularity, global comparison geometry, advanced turbulence and noncommutative harmonic analysis. These require individual inclusion or justified depth-specific deferral during repair rather than being treated as implicitly covered.
practiceNotes: Flashcards support retrieval, discrimination and preparation; proof writing, programming, modeling and experimental competence require the extended practice specified in each deck.

Chemical, biological and physical laboratory work requires local training, supervision, risk assessment, appropriate facilities and approved waste-handling procedures; these conditions are not represented as already satisfied.
Human-participant studies, identifiable biological data, animal work and regulated field collection may require institutional ethics review, consent, permits and data-governance approval.
Radiation, high-voltage, laser and specialized instrument work requires facility-specific authorization and safety procedures; public datasets and simulations can support non-operational practice.
Security experiments must use explicitly authorized, isolated systems. Robotics hardware experiments require controlled environments and independent safety review before autonomous operation.
Synthetic-biology practice is limited to appropriately reviewed, low-risk educational systems; containment approval and environmental-release authorization are separate from curriculum knowledge.
